question: A honeybee queen mates with about a dozen males. On average, how related is a worker to a sister chosen at random?
answer: About three tenths. Sisters with the same father share three quarters of their genes, because a male passes on his whole genome; sisters with different fathers share a quarter. With a dozen fathers, most sisters are half-sisters, and the average falls to about 0.3, below the half a worker would share with her own young.
move: The figure for the closest pair is not the average of the group.
trap: Using the full-sister figure without asking how many fathers there were.
source: Crozier & Pamilo, Evolution of Social Insect Colonies
reference: Crozier & Pamilo, Evolution of Social Insect Colonies: Sex Allocation and Kin Selection, Oxford University Press, 1996
